Introduction

REST API for the MW Realty mobile app: property search, listings, agents, content, customer accounts, enquiries and the AI assistant.

Base URL: http://localhost 
The same API the website uses. All responses are JSON. Example responses for `GET` endpoints were recorded from real data, so field names and nesting are exact.

## Headers

Send these on every request:

| Header | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `Accept` | `application/json` | Errors always come back as JSON. |
| `X-Device-Id` | A random id (16–60 letters, digits or `-`, e.g. a UUID) the app creates on first launch and keeps | Identifies the device for the AI chat, enquiry history and listing stats, in place of the website's cookie. Without it the AI chat cannot continue a conversation and screen views are not recorded. |
| `Authorization` | `Bearer {token}` | Only when a customer is signed in. Required for the **Customer Account** endpoints; optional elsewhere (enquiries sent with it appear in the customer's account). |
| `User-Agent` | Your app's name/version | Requests without one are treated as bots and not tracked. |

## Signing in

1. **Sign up:** `POST /api/auth/register` → emails a 4-digit code → `POST /api/auth/verify-otp` returns a `token`.
2. **Sign in:** `POST /api/auth/login` (email + password) or `POST /api/auth/google` (access token from the native Google Sign-In SDK) returns a `token`.
3. Store the token securely (Keychain / Keystore) and send it as `Authorization: Bearer {token}`. Tokens don't expire; `POST /api/auth/logout` revokes the current one.
4. A `401` on an authenticated endpoint means the token is no longer valid: clear it and show the sign-in screen.

## Language and currency

* `GET /api/languages` lists the languages (currently `en` and `ar`). Send `?lang={code}` on content endpoints; titles, descriptions and labels come back translated.
* `GET /api/static-translations?lang={code}` returns the UI copy (button labels etc.).
* Every price is in **AED**. `GET /api/currencies` returns exchange `rate`s (units per 1 AED) for display conversion.

## Pagination

Paginated lists return a `pagination` object: `current_page`, `last_page` and usually `total`. Request the next page with `?page=N` until `current_page == last_page`.

## Errors

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `401` | Missing or invalid token | `{"message": "Unauthenticated."}` |
| `404` | Not found (e.g. unpublished listing) | `{"message": "Not found"}` |
| `422` | Validation failed | `{"message": "…", "errors": {"field": ["…"]}}`: show `errors` next to each field |
| `429` | Too many requests | Wait for the `Retry-After` header (seconds) |

## Rate limits (per IP)

Sign-in: 5/min per email, 30/min overall · Sign-up: 10/hour · OTP: 8/min · Forms and enquiries: 20/hour · AI chat: 8/min and 150/day · Location autocomplete and map: 120/min.

## Forms and reCAPTCHA

The website protects forms (enquiries, viewings, downloads, contact, newsletter, careers, chat details) with Google reCAPTCHA v3 through the `recaptcha_token` field. **While reCAPTCHA is enabled on the server, these endpoints answer `422` with `errors.recaptcha_token` when the field is missing.** Sign-in, sign-up and the customer account endpoints don't use it. How the app will pass this check is still open; agree on it with the backend team before building the forms.

## Images and files

Image fields (`image`, `images`, `avatar_url`, `logo_url` …) are absolute URLs. A brochure or floor plan `download_url` is a signed link valid for 15 minutes and needs no token.

Authenticating requests

To authenticate requests, include an Authorization header with the value "Bearer {YOUR_TOKEN}".

All authenticated endpoints are marked with a requires authentication badge in the documentation below.

Get a token from POST /api/auth/login, /api/auth/verify-otp or /api/auth/google, and send it as Authorization: Bearer {token}.

App Config

Languages

The languages content is available in. Send the chosen code as ?lang= on every request.

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost/api/languages" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --header "X-Device-Id: {DEVICE_ID}"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/api/languages"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "X-Device-Id": "{DEVICE_ID}",
};


fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
}).then(response => response.json());

Currencies

Prices from every endpoint are in AED; to display another currency, multiply by its rate (units per 1 AED).

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost/api/currencies" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --header "X-Device-Id: {DEVICE_ID}"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/api/currencies"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "X-Device-Id": "{DEVICE_ID}",
};


fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
}).then(response => response.json());

UI translations

Static UI copy (labels, buttons…) as a key → text map for one language. Cache it on the device per language.

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost/api/static-translations?lang=en" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --header "X-Device-Id: {DEVICE_ID}"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/api/static-translations"
);

const params = {
    "lang": "en",
};
Object.keys(params)
    .forEach(key => url.searchParams.append(key, params[key]));

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "X-Device-Id": "{DEVICE_ID}",
};


fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
}).then(response => response.json());

Search & Filters

Public read-only endpoint the frontend (home banner + /properties listing) uses to render the search filter bar. Options come straight from the admin-managed filters/filter_values tables, so a new filter or option shows up here without a code change. Option counts and slider bounds use the listings of the page asking: residential by default, or ?scope=commercial for /commercial.

Search filter bar

The filters to render (selects with their options and live listing counts, number sliders with min/max/step), in admin order. Pass the chosen values back to the listing endpoints under each filter's key.

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost/api/property-filters?page=listing&scope=residential&lang=en" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --header "X-Device-Id: {DEVICE_ID}" \
    --data "{
    \"page\": \"listing\",
    \"lang\": \"vmqeopfuu\",
    \"scope\": \"residential\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/api/property-filters"
);

const params = {
    "page": "listing",
    "scope": "residential",
    "lang": "en",
};
Object.keys(params)
    .forEach(key => url.searchParams.append(key, params[key]));

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "X-Device-Id": "{DEVICE_ID}",
};

let body = {
    "page": "listing",
    "lang": "vmqeopfuu",
    "scope": "residential"
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Location autocomplete

Cities, communities and addresses matching what the user typed (2+ characters; fewer returns an empty list). Pass a picked suggestion back as city= / community= / location= on the listing endpoints. Debounce on the client — limited to 120 calls/minute.

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost/api/location-suggestions?q=mar&scope=all&lang=en" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --header "X-Device-Id: {DEVICE_ID}" \
    --data "{
    \"q\": \"vmqeopfuudtdsufvyvddq\",
    \"lang\": \"amniihfqc\",
    \"scope\": \"commercial\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/api/location-suggestions"
);

const params = {
    "q": "mar",
    "scope": "all",
    "lang": "en",
};
Object.keys(params)
    .forEach(key => url.searchParams.append(key, params[key]));

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "X-Device-Id": "{DEVICE_ID}",
};

let body = {
    "q": "vmqeopfuudtdsufvyvddq",
    "lang": "amniihfqc",
    "scope": "commercial"
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --header "X-Device-Id: {DEVICE_ID}"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/api/properties"
);

const params = {
    "lang": "en",
    "page": "1",
};
Object.keys(params)
    .forEach(key => url.searchParams.append(key, params[key]));

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "X-Device-Id": "{DEVICE_ID}",
};


fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
}).then(response => response.json());

Request failed with error:


Tip: Check that you're properly connected to the network.
If you're a maintainer of ths API, verify that your API is running and you've enabled CORS.

Request      

GET api/properties/{slug}

Headers

Content-Type        

Example: application/json

Accept        

Example: application/json

X-Device-Id        

Example: {DEVICE_ID}

URL Parameters

slug   string     

The listing slug from a property card. Example: virella-2

Query Parameters

lang   string  optional    

Example: en

Agents & Agencies

Public, read-only endpoints for the /agents listing page and /agent-details/{slug} page.

List agents

Without per_page every agent is returned (the website's behaviour); pass per_page to page through them and get a pagination block.

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost/api/agents?lang=en&per_page=20&page=1" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --header "X-Device-Id: {DEVICE_ID}"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/api/agents"
);

const params = {
    "lang": "en",
    "per_page": "20",
    "page": "1",
};
Object.keys(params)
    .forEach(key => url.searchParams.append(key, params[key]));

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "X-Device-Id": "{DEVICE_ID}",
};


fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
}).then(response => response.json());

Leads & Enquiries

Property enquiry

"Contact agent" form on a listing — goes to the listing's agent/agency CRM. If a customer token is sent, the enquiry also appears under their account.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost/api/leads/capture" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --header "X-Device-Id: {DEVICE_ID}" \
    --data "{
    \"property_id\": 111,
    \"name\": \"Sara Ahmed\",
    \"email\": \"buyer@example.com\",
    \"phone\": \"501234567\",
    \"phone_country_code\": \"+971\",
    \"company\": \"mniihfqcoynlazghdtqtq\",
    \"country\": \"xbajwbpilpmufinllwloa\",
    \"message\": \"Is this still available? I\'d like to view it this week.\",
    \"page_source\": \"mobile-app\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/api/leads/capture"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "X-Device-Id": "{DEVICE_ID}",
};

let body = {
    "property_id": 111,
    "name": "Sara Ahmed",
    "email": "buyer@example.com",
    "phone": "501234567",
    "phone_country_code": "+971",
    "company": "mniihfqcoynlazghdtqtq",
    "country": "xbajwbpilpmufinllwloa",
    "message": "Is this still available? I'd like to view it this week.",
    "page_source": "mobile-app"
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Book a viewing

A property lead (same routing as an enquiry) with the requested day + time slot. If the listing has open house days (available_dates on the property details), only those days are accepted; otherwise any day from today up to 60 days ahead.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost/api/leads/viewing" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --header "X-Device-Id: {DEVICE_ID}" \
    --data "{
    \"property_id\": 111,
    \"name\": \"Sara Ahmed\",
    \"email\": \"buyer@example.com\",
    \"phone\": \"501234567\",
    \"phone_country_code\": \"+971\",
    \"viewing_date\": \"2026-10-15\",
    \"viewing_time\": \"afternoon\",
    \"note\": \"Please call before coming.\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/api/leads/viewing"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "X-Device-Id": "{DEVICE_ID}",
};

let body = {
    "property_id": 111,
    "name": "Sara Ahmed",
    "email": "buyer@example.com",
    "phone": "501234567",
    "phone_country_code": "+971",
    "viewing_date": "2026-10-15",
    "viewing_time": "afternoon",
    "note": "Please call before coming."
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Send a message

Ask the AI assistant. The reply may include matching property cards. Limited to 8 messages/minute and 150/day per IP.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost/api/chatbot/message" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --header "X-Device-Id: {DEVICE_ID}" \
    --data "{
    \"message\": \"Show me 2 bedroom apartments in Dubai Marina under 2M\",
    \"lang\": \"en\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/api/chatbot/message"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "X-Device-Id": "{DEVICE_ID}",
};

let body = {
    "message": "Show me 2 bedroom apartments in Dubai Marina under 2M",
    "lang": "en"
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Tracking

Screen view

Call when a screen opens. Send the website path the screen corresponds to — that is how views are classified: /property-details/{slug} = property view (counts towards the listing's stats and routes the visitor to its agent), /properties?bedrooms=2&... = a search, anything else = a page view. Keep the returned id to report time spent.

Requires the X-Device-Id header (nothing is recorded without it).

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost/api/track/page" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --header "X-Device-Id: {DEVICE_ID}" \
    --data "{
    \"path\": \"\\/property-details\\/virella-2\",
    \"title\": \"Virella 2\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/api/track/page"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "X-Device-Id": "{DEVICE_ID}",
};

let body = {
    "path": "\/property-details\/virella-2",
    "title": "Virella 2"
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

requires authentication

Send as multipart/form-data when uploading an avatar. Use POST from the app — PHP does not parse file uploads on PUT (the PUT route is kept for the website).

Example request:
curl --request PUT \
    "http://localhost/api/customer/settings" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_TOKEN}" \
    --header "Content-Type: multipart/form-data" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --header "X-Device-Id: {DEVICE_ID}" \
    --form "name=Sara Ahmed"\
    --form "email=buyer@example.com"\
    --form "phone=+971 50 123 4567"\
    --form "location=Dubai Marina"\
    --form "password=newSecret123"\
    --form "password_confirmation=newSecret123"\
    --form "avatar=@C:\Users\User\AppData\Local\Temp\php6D6F.tmp" 
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/api/customer/settings"
);

const headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer {YOUR_TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "multipart/form-data",
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "X-Device-Id": "{DEVICE_ID}",
};

const body = new FormData();
body.append('name', 'Sara Ahmed');
body.append('email', 'buyer@example.com');
body.append('phone', '+971 50 123 4567');
body.append('location', 'Dubai Marina');
body.append('password', 'newSecret123');
body.append('password_confirmation', 'newSecret123');
body.append('avatar', document.querySelector('input[name="avatar"]').files[0]);

fetch(url, {
    method: "PUT",
    headers,
    body,
}).then(response => response.json());

User Auth

Token (Bearer) auth for the mobile app's User account (buyers/visitors). Agents and agencies don't sign in through these endpoints.

Same accounts, OTP and Google rules as the website's session login (Customer\CustomerAuthController) — the only difference is that a successful sign-in returns a Sanctum token instead of a cookie.

Send the token on every authenticated request: Authorization: Bearer {token}.

Sign up

Step 1 of sign-up. Creates the account and emails a 4-digit code — no token yet; call POST /api/auth/verify-otp with the returned user_id and the code. email_sent: false means the email failed — offer "Resend code".

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost/api/auth/register" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --header "X-Device-Id: {DEVICE_ID}" \
    --data "{
    \"name\": \"Sara Ahmed\",
    \"email\": \"buyer@example.com\",
    \"phone\": \"501234567\",
    \"phone_country_code\": \"+971\",
    \"password\": \"secret123\",
    \"password_confirmation\": \"secret123\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/api/auth/register"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "X-Device-Id": "{DEVICE_ID}",
};

let body = {
    "name": "Sara Ahmed",
    "email": "buyer@example.com",
    "phone": "501234567",
    "phone_country_code": "+971",
    "password": "secret123",
    "password_confirmation": "secret123"
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Verify sign-up code

Step 2 of sign-up: the 4-digit code emailed by POST /api/auth/register. Marks the email verified and returns a Bearer token.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost/api/auth/verify-otp" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --header "X-Device-Id: {DEVICE_ID}" \
    --data "{
    \"user_id\": 7,
    \"code\": \"1234\",
    \"device_name\": \"Pixel 8\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/api/auth/verify-otp"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "X-Device-Id": "{DEVICE_ID}",
};

let body = {
    "user_id": 7,
    "code": "1234",
    "device_name": "Pixel 8"
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Example response (200):


{
    "token": "12|9xQ...",
    "token_type": "Bearer",
    "user": {
        "id": 7,
        "name": "Sara Ahmed",
        "email": "buyer@example.com",
        "phone": null,
        "location": null,
        "avatar_url": null,
        "email_verified": true
    }
}

Example response (422):


{
    "message": "Invalid or expired code."
}

Continue with Google

Exchange the access token from the native Google Sign-In SDK for an app token. Links to an existing account with the same email, or creates one. For the User account only — agents and agencies don't have Google sign-in (show the button only on the User tab).

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost/api/auth/google" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --header "X-Device-Id: {DEVICE_ID}" \
    --data "{
    \"access_token\": \"ya29.a0Af...\",
    \"device_name\": \"iPhone 15 Pro\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/api/auth/google"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "X-Device-Id": "{DEVICE_ID}",
};

let body = {
    "access_token": "ya29.a0Af...",
    "device_name": "iPhone 15 Pro"
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Example response (200):


{
    "token": "12|9xQ...",

Sign out

requires authentication

Revokes the token used for this request (other devices stay signed in).

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost/api/auth/logout" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_TOKEN}" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --header "X-Device-Id: {DEVICE_ID}"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost/api/auth/logout"
);

const headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer {YOUR_TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "X-Device-Id": "{DEVICE_ID}",
};


fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
}).then(response => response.json());
